transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], The Drowned Priest [T-04].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain needles down in grey sheets as you crest the last rise and see it: Hollowmoot, hunched on its pilings above black water, lanterns swaying like drunk fireflies. Between you and the town gate, the Ashwater Causeway narrows to a single plank track, and at its foot a Warden checkpoint has backed up a ragged line of refugees, mules and handcarts. A woman in a rain-slicked warden's coat walks the queue with a ledger and a hooked pole, marking names, taking coin, turning some away toward the dark. Somewhere behind you, faint under the rain, you can just about convince yourself you don't hear a tuneless, swarming hum drifting off the flooded lowlands. The water at the causeway's edge is already lapping over the old high-water marks carved into the stone.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: That causeway won't hold much longer if the water keeps rising. Are you truly turning folk back toward those waters?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde works her way through the queue toward the Warden with the practiced ease of someone used to navigating tight spaces and tense situations. She glances at the water lapping against the causeway's ancient marks—reading them like a river—then turns her full attention to the woman with the ledger, her expression serious.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: That rain's telling me something—watch how it falls in sheets, then stops all sudden, thick as drowning breath. The water's not just rising. Something's driving it.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (I break from the queue and move to the causeway's edge, where the black water laps and froths. I tilt my face to the falling rain, reading its rhythm and weight, my hands held out to feel it speak. The pattern in those needles tells me more than a ledger ever could.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: There's logic to who she's letting through. I need to know what it is before we approach.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen pulls her cloak tighter against the rain and studies the checkpoint with practiced eyes—watching how Warden Pell marks her ledger, which refugees she turns toward the dark and which she waves through, reading the body language and the method behind the chaos. She positions herself in the crowd where she can observe without drawing attention, cataloging the pattern.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: That sound... that's not the rain, is it? And that Warden's looking for more than names in that ledger.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire hangs back from the main queue, her eyes tracking the Warden's patterns—where she looks, which refugees she marks, how long she lets each one argue. The rain helps; she's just another hunched figure among dozens. Her hand stays loose at her side, ready, while she listens beneath the downpour for that sound again, trying to place it. Guard's work, the kind they taught her at the orphanage that never leaves your bones.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: —No. No, that's not the Barge again, that's just rain and tide.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - - - 0, invoking Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01] → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Notice: dice - - 0 -, invoking Stands against the Wardens' torches [MO-03] → Average (+1) vs Average (+1): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice - 0 - +, invoking Trained young in watch drills [MI-01] → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen reads the pattern in Pell's ledger just fine—but as she does, somewhere up on the stilts the watchtower bell starts clanging, quarantine-fashion. Pell's head snaps up and the whole line goes tense, warden spears leveling toward the crowd; Morwen still has her read on the checkpoint's logic, but now every eye at the checkpoint is on the refugees, hers included, and she'll have to move fast before the Wardens start dragging people out of line for inspection.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The rain confirms what Aldous already feared — this isn't weather, it's a tide with intent, the drops falling too heavy, too rhythmic, like something breathing under the marsh (he holds that ill omen close, a warning he can lean on later). Morwen's read on Pell's ledger clicks into place — she can see exactly who gets waved through and who gets turned — but the instant she has it, the watchtower bell starts hammering out its quarantine clang, and Sergeant Pell's head snaps up. Spears level across the queue; the crowd flinches as one animal. Mire, though, has been watching longer and closer than anyone — in the scramble as Wardens push toward the line to start dragging people out for inspection, she clocks the one gap in their formation, the blind stretch of planking nobody's covering yet. Ysolde is still at Pell's shoulder, ledger and hooked pole inches away, and now has a warden sergeant with spears rising all around her and a straight question hanging in the rain: does she press Pell right now, before the checkpoint locks down entirely, or does the party use Mire's gap and go?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Look at me, Sergeant. Look at those water marks. I know what I'm reading, and you know I wouldn't ask if it wasn't true. Get these people through now.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde is still at Pell's shoulder, close enough to make this personal. She meets the Warden's eyes directly while gesturing toward the rising water, her voice cutting through the chaos with the authority of someone who's read both tides and people for years. She's not begging—she's calling on Pell's real duty: to protect these refugees from what's actually coming.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The water's being *driven*—I read it in the rain! Something's coming through the flood, and that causeway won't hold past midnight!

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous straightens at the causeway edge where he's been reading the rain, water spray beading on his weathered coat. As chaos erupts around the checkpoint—spears rising, Wardens shouting—he raises his voice, raw and certain, and points down at the black water that's already climbing wrong-fast against the stone.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Warden Pell—I can read your ledger too. You're not just checking names. What are you really looking for before this checkpoint becomes something darker?

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward from the crowd to stand with Ysolde, rain drumming off her cloak. Her eyes track Pell's movements, reading the weight in every mark, every turned-away face. She's seen the pattern—now she wants the truth. There's no threat in her voice, only certainty and the steady presence of someone who has seen what happens when Wardens panic without reason.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Gap on the north side—move now, I'll cover you.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire shifts through the crowd, planting herself with a clear sight line to both the opening and the checkpoint. She catches her companions' eyes in quick succession, one hand raised to point the way, her body language all coiled readiness—the stance of a guard holding the line, even disgraced.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I—the water, it's—

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Your faith honors me, but I can't save anyone who drowns on this causeway—move through now, while there's still time. I'll be in Hollowmoot. Go.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Empathy: dice + - - 0, invoking Reads river currents like kin [YS-01] → Superb (+5) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde holds Pell's stare through the rain and doesn't blink, and something in the sergeant's face gives way — not mercy exactly, but recognition. Pell looks past Ysolde at the black water climbing over the old high-marks, at Aldous still shouting about a tide with intent, and makes her call: "Move them! Now, before the bell locks it down proper!" The line lurches forward all at once, spears lowering, Wardens herding rather than hunting. In the crush Aldous's warning about the driven water earns him nothing but shoves and cold looks — he takes it hard, the ghosts of the Sunken Barge pressing close as the crowd's panic brushes too near his own. Morwen, caught between the surge and a knot of frightened pilgrims who recognize her face and cling to her sleeve, has to choose the crowd over her own footing, losing precious seconds she can't get back. Mire's gap holds true, though — she walks the whole party through the blind stretch of planking she marked, past a hunched figure mending a hull under a lean-to (a boatwright, mute, hands flying in quick unmistakable signs — *hurry* — before he vanishes back to his dry work) and a wiry runner who slips along a rooftop line above the queue, coded and quick, gone before anyone can call out to her. Soaked, jostled, and short of breath, the four of you clear the checkpoint and step up onto Hollowmoot's swaying stilts as the quarantine bell finally locks the causeway shut behind you — the Ashwater is closed for the night, and you're on the right side of it.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Senna, a Blackwater Cartel enforcer — the same crew that takes hostages for leverage along the fords — corners the party in a rain-black alley off the stilt-walk, her spear-hook lowered but her hands shaking. begs the party to go to the hidden cellars the Cartel smuggles through under Wick Lane, where Senna says she can buy the party a way through — but only if they help her first., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The alley is barely wider than your shoulders, black water sheeting off the eaves above, and Senna steps out of it like she's been waiting since before you cleared the checkpoint — hook-spear low, but her knuckles white on the haft and her voice cracking on the first word. She doesn't threaten. She begs: her boy went out three nights ago chasing that hum under the rain and hasn't come back, and she knows where the cellars run under Wick Lane, knows a way through the Cartel's watch that could get you clear of Hollowmoot's checkpoints for good — but she won't give you the way until someone helps her get him back, or at least find out what's left of him. Behind her, faint and constant under the rain, that same tuneless swarm-song threads up from the direction of the drowned temple.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Your son is caught by something older than fear. We'll find him—I swear it. Show us where to look.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward through the rain-black alley without hesitation, closing the distance between herself and Senna. She meets the woman's eyes directly, her expression steady and unflinching, recognizing the desperation of someone willing to walk into danger for her child. She's already decided.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The song in the rain—that's the thing that's been drowning us. Your boy didn't wander up there alone, Senna. That hum was calling him, and I've been reading it since the causeway. Show me where he went.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward without hesitation, rain streaming down his weathered face. His hand reaches out—not threatening, but intent—toward the direction Senna indicated. The swarm-song threading up from the drowned temple is the same tune he's been reading in the rain all night, the same omen that marked the Sunken Barge. He doesn't negotiate or wait; he's already moving, already committed to following it to its source. This is what he reads omens for—to walk toward the things that terrify everyone else.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Your son heard the song and it called to him—I know that pull, even for those it touches. Tell me everything: when he left, what he was doing, what you've seen and heard since. I've come back from worse than this. So can he.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward without fear, her posture calm and her hands open. She meets Senna's desperate gaze steadily, the rain streaming off her dark cloak. There is no judgment in her face—only the quiet certainty of someone who has walked this darkness before and knows what must be asked.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Your boy followed that hum three nights ago? Then he's already changed, or he's already gone—but I know the cellars under Wick Lane. Help me understand what we're walking into, and I'll help you walk back out of it alive.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward slowly, hands open and visible, reading Senna's grip on the spear-haft and the genuine terror in her face. She's seen desperate parents before—she was raised without one. She plants her feet in that alley stance, the one taught at the orphanage watch drills, and her voice comes low and steady: not threatening, but all business.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Tell them Mire vouched for it. The debt only grows anyway—might as well make it count for something real.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Senna's shoulders drop like a cut line when all four of you commit at once — Ysolde's oath, Aldous's grim certainty about the song, Morwen's steady questions, Mire's flat promise to walk her back out alive. She talks fast now, rain running off her chin: her boy's name is Corin, eleven years old, gone three nights following that hum, last seen near the old flood-stair behind Wick Lane. She presses a slick iron key into Mire's palm — the cellar hatch — and says the Cartel won't touch you going in if Mire's name is on it. Mire takes the weight of that without flinching, knowing full well what it means: her debt to the Blackwater Cartel just grew teeth again, her name now bound to whatever this costs. Senna leads you deeper into the alley, toward the black stair down into Wick Lane's cellars, the swarm-song rising faint and constant from the drowned temple beyond the rooftops — you're leaving the causeway and the open road behind for good.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The iron key turns easy in a hatch worn smooth by a hundred smugglers' hands, and Senna leads you down a ladder into air that smells of tallow, brine, and old sacking. Wick Lane's cellars run on and on beneath the stilts, a warren of dry-stacked crates and low brick arches, lantern-light picking out chalk marks on the walls that aren't Cartel code — spirals, the same shape over and over, scratched low near the floor like something small and frightened drew them at knee height. Senna's breath goes ragged every time the swarm-song swells faintly through the stone, and she won't look at a locked side-door near the back, the one with fresh scratches around its frame. Somewhere past it, water is moving that shouldn't be — a hatch to the river, maybe, or something using one.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Senna, look at these marks—he was still thinking, still fighting. This isn't someone just lost to the song.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves to the spiral marks scratched at knee height along the cellar wall. She crouches down to examine them without touching, reading each scratch like she reads the voices of her crew during the night watches—understanding fear and intention beneath the surface. The marks are deliberate, repeated. This is the work of someone trying to leave a message, still thinking even as something old was calling him into the dark.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: That water's not just moving—it's singing. The same song your boy heard. Show me what's behind that door, Senna, or I'll open it myself.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves toward the locked side-door without hesitation, his weathered hand hovering over the fresh scratches carved in the frame. He tilts his head toward the sound of water moving beyond—not the mindless flood, but something rhythmic and intentional—and his jaw tightens as he reads it. Beneath the mechanical lap and hiss, the swarm-song threads through: the same omen that marked the Sunken Barge, the same call that drew the boy into the dark. He's read this before, written in drowning breath and rising tides. The door doesn't hold back water. It holds back the thing that *uses* the water as its voice.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: He was here for days, fighting it the whole time, until something broke or changed. I've called people back from the song's edge before, Senna—but I need to know what state he's in when we find him. What's behind that door?

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen kneels before the spirals scratched into the stone at knee height, her fingers brushing each obsessive loop. She reads in them the slow, terrible progression of hive-touch taking hold—the moment when a child stops fighting and accepts what's calling to him from the dark. She rises with the certainty of someone who has walked this threshold before and knows what each mark means. Her gaze turns to the locked door Senna won't face.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Those scratches are at knee-height—a frightened child made them. The water's being driven from below, and the song's coming with it. This door's holding something back, and we need to know what before it breaks.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward to examine the locked door with methodical precision—the kind of careful, tactical reading she was trained for since childhood in the orphanage watch drills. She traces the fresh scratches around its frame, her fingertips finding grooves at knee-height, small and desperate. The water beyond moves with wrong-rhythm, and she listens intently to the swarm-song threading through the stone, reading it like she read the checkpoint guards. Threat assessment. Understanding exactly what waits and what it will cost to open.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The water... it's the same cadence, the same breath as the Barge going down. No—*no*. That's not the drowned dark, that's Corin on the other side. The boy is still there, still calling. I can read it.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 0 0 + → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Lore: dice 0 + + + → Fantastic (+6) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice + 0 + -, invoking Trained young in watch drills [MI-01] → Fantastic (+6) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The three of you read the door like a shared held breath — and the shape of it comes clear all at once. Aldous's hand steadies over the scratches: the rhythm beyond isn't the drowned dark's slow breathing, it's *wrong* in a way that means a living thing is still fighting it, still keeping its own time against the swarm-song's pull — he'd stake the ghosts of the Sunken Barge on it (**Reads the Omen in the Moving Water**). Morwen straightens from the spirals with cold certainty: these are the marks of a boy still resisting, days deep, the progression not yet complete — she knows exactly what state to expect when that door opens, and what it will take to pull him back (**Reading Corin's Descent**). Mire's fingers trace the frame's fresh gouges and she places it precisely — the song isn't coming *through* the door, it's coming *from below* it, up through the water itself, meaning whatever's driving the tide down there is close, patient, and listening right now (**The Song Comes From Below**). Senna sways where she stands, one hand pressed to her mouth, staring at the door she still won't touch — she believes you now, all the way down, and that terror is its own kind of confirmation. The lock waits. Behind it: water that shouldn't move the way it moves, and somewhere in it, a boy who hasn't stopped fighting yet.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Senna. Corin's still in there, still fighting—we all read it in those scratches. He hasn't broken. He's waiting for his mother to come get him.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde closes the distance between herself and Senna in three quick steps, reaching out to grip the woman's shoulders firmly—not rough, but grounding. She steps directly into Senna's line of sight and holds it, the way she held Pell's at the checkpoint. Her voice comes quiet and absolute beneath the distant swarm-song.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Open it. That boy's still himself on the other side—still fighting—and the song won't wait much longer.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous places his weathered hand on the frame where Corin's desperate scratches mark the stone. He doesn't wait for permission or debate—he steps toward Mire with absolute certainty, his eyes meeting hers, and nods once: sharp and commanding. Open it now, or he goes through by force. The weight of his conviction fills the cellar like water, and there's no hesitation left in him, only the terrible certainty of someone who has read the omens and decided what comes next.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You still have your name, Corin. Your will is still your own. I'm coming to bring you home.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward to the locked door, her hands moving in the precise, practiced gestures of a rite that predates the Order's teachings by centuries. Her voice drops into an older cadence—syllables that carry weight and purpose, speaking not commands but invitations. She traces patterns in the still air, drawing at something half-lost and desperate on the other side of the stone. The swamp-water beyond seems to hold its breath as she works.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The hatch is close to failing anyway—if we don't open it now, it opens for us. Back by the arch. When I turn the key, anything that comes through gets through me first.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire positions her companions with quick hand signals, the orphanage-taught precision that never left her, moving them back to defensive ground by the brick arch. She plants herself square before the locked door, one hand settling on the iron key, her body language all coiled readiness. She's read the water-rhythm and the wrong-cadence beneath the swarm-song enough to know what's waiting. Not perfectly—but enough. She turns the key.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Lore: dice + 0 - + → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's rite finds its shape all at once — the old syllables catching like a hook in still water, and something on the other side of the door *answers*. Not words. A shift in the water's rhythm, a fractional slowing, as if a small drowning thing just heard its own name spoken by someone who means to keep it. The working settles over the cellar like a held note, ready to be called on the instant that door swings wide (**A Rite of Calling Back**). Senna makes a sound she probably didn't mean to make — half sob, half prayer — and presses both hands to her mouth. Behind her, Mire's grip tightens on the iron key, already seated in the lock, the others braced at the arch exactly where she placed them. The swarm-song swells once, low and patient, from somewhere beneath the stone. The key only needs to turn.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Mire and I are taking what comes through. Senna, keep close to Morwen—your son is still himself in there, and we're bringing him home.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves to stand directly beside Mire at the locked door, her shoulders squared to face whatever waits on the other side. She's positioned her body between Senna and the threshold—a living barrier of commitment. Her hand rests on the stone frame, feeling the scratches Corin left behind, the small desperate marks of a boy still fighting in the dark. She's read crew secrets in the night watches; she knows how to listen beneath words to what truly calls. Now she listens to the water moving beyond this door and prepares to meet whatever answers when Mire turns the key.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The boy is still there. The song can't have him while he's still fighting—and I've read every mark he left behind. Turn it now, or I turn it myself.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward through the breath-held silence and places his weathered hand over Mire's on the iron key. He doesn't wait, doesn't hesitate—he turns it with the absolute certainty of someone who has read the omens and knows what must come next. The lock gives way beneath his palm with a click that echoes through the cellar like a held breath finally released. Whatever waits on the other side has been patient long enough.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Hold fast to your own name, Corin—I have you now. The song can't touch what's being called back into itself.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen holds the rite steady as Mire's hand tightens on the key, maintaining the older syllables and the precise hand-patterns that keep the working open like a door swinging both ways. As the lock begins to turn, she doesn't step forward—she *pulls*, drawing the weight of her calling through the threshold like a fishing line gone taut, ready to bring the boy back toward the light and the hands that will hold him safe when he crosses.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Hold your ground. Nothing gets past me.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire turns the iron key all the way through, feeling it click open beneath her palm. She plants herself square in front of the door, every muscle coiled and ready, one hand shifting to grip the door's edge. She's held worse thresholds than this alone—held them under fire, held them through panic. This she understands: the weight of position, the cost of holding it, the certainty that comes with training and the absolute knowledge of exactly what she can do.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The key turns, the door gives — and the cellar exhales. Black water sheets out over the threshold in a single cold wave, and below it a flooded stair drops away into dark, the swarm-song rising sudden and close, no longer muffled by stone. Clinging to the last dry step, half-submerged, is a boy: pale, fever-bright, lips moving around the tuneless hum even as his whole body shakes trying not to answer it. Morwen's rite goes taut like a hooked line the instant she says his name again — *Corin* — and something in the water resists, a slow drag against her pull, before the boy's own hand finds the doorframe on his own strength. Ysolde and Mire hold the threshold as something unseen lashes up out of the black behind him — not a limb so much as an absence, a wrongness in the water's shape — and recoils when it meets Mire's braced stance and Ysolde's grip hauling Corin the rest of the way through. Aldous drags him the final foot onto dry stone, reading the boy's ragged, off-cadence breathing against the swarm-song's rhythm and confirming what the marks already told them: still himself, still fighting, marked but not lost. Senna goes down on her knees in the flood-runoff, sobbing his name into his soaked hair, and behind them all the song swells once, hard and patient, like something enormous just noticed exactly what was taken from it. The door won't shut again without a fight — Mire wedges it as best she can — but Corin is out, breathing, and Senna presses the promised route through Wick Lane into your hands with shaking gratitude, whispering that the Cartel will let you pass now, on her word and on what you did for her boy.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Senna carries Corin up out of the flood-stair wrapped in someone's cloak, and the party follows her deeper into the Wick Lane warren rather than back up to the rain — she says her word is only good if she says it to the right ears. The cellars widen ahead into a proper smuggler's hold: dry-stacked crates, lantern-oil, the low murmur of night-barge business going on as usual, utterly indifferent to what just came up from the water. A wiry man with a ledger and a rival lieutenant's watchful stare meets you at the threshold, already having heard through the warren's whispers that Senna's debt just changed shape. He's willing to make good on her promise — the route north, past the checkpoints, quiet and dry — but he wants to know exactly what you dragged out of that stairwell, and what it means for cargo the Cartel still has moving through these same flooded tunnels. Somewhere behind you, faint through the stone, the swarm-song has not stopped.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: What came up from that stairwell was hive-touched and singing — it had claimed the boy, but not completely, not yet. There's something down there in the flooded dark that uses the water like a voice, and it was using your cellars to reach deeper into the warren. It's sealed below now. Your cargo moving through those tunnels is safer than it was an hour ago — and your people can trust us with that knowledge.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward to address the wiry man directly, positioning herself protectively near Senna while meeting his gaze. She speaks with the calm certainty of someone who has managed crew and read people through long night watches — honest, direct, and strategic about what the Cartel needs to hear.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: That song marked the boy for three days before we pulled him out. It's still singing through your cellars. What does the Cartel know about what's down there—and how many others have you run through it?

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps into the wiry man's space without hesitation, reading him like he reads omens in floodwater—the calculation in the ledger, the watchfulness, the way this is all cargo and accounting to him. His weathered hand is still damp from the black. When he speaks, his voice carries the certainty of someone who has read every mark Corin left scratched into the stone, who felt the wrongness in water that resisted being survived. He doesn't ask permission. He never does.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You have something in your tunnels that isn't just water or flood-tide. It takes people slowly—it hums until they follow it down. The boy lasted three days before we pulled him back. That thing down there doesn't lose what it claims easily, and it will still be hungry when the tides turn again. You should want us gone north quickly, because the longer we stay, the more attention gets drawn to these cellars.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward to meet the wiry man's gaze directly, her dark cloak still dripping from the cellar waters. She doesn't flinch from his question—there's no deception in her face, only the steady certainty of someone speaking truth that the Cartel needs to hear. She gestures back toward the stairwell where the swarm-song still murmurs faintly through the stone.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: We pulled the boy out clean—he's what mattered. What's in that water now knows your tunnels too. That's between you and whatever's waiting down there.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward to meet the lieutenant at the threshold, her weight settled and her hands visible—that militia stance learned young in the orphanage watch drills. She reads his watchful stare and his calculation: is this good for operations or a problem? She answers with flat certainty, offering facts without volunteering more than necessary. She knows her debt to the Cartel just got more visible, and she's watching exactly how he means to measure it.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ferro listens to all four of you without writing a word, his eyes flicking once toward the rival lieutenant hovering at his shoulder — a lean, sharp-jawed woman who's said nothing but hasn't stopped watching Mire since the word "debt" changed hands. When you finish, Ferro closes the ledger with a soft snap. "Senna's word is good," he says, "and so, it seems, is yours." He waves two barge-hands forward to open the dry route north — quiet tunnels, no tolls, no checkpoints, exactly as promised. But the rival lieutenant leans in before he's done, murmuring something about how a debt that changes shape once can change shape twice, her gaze never leaving Mire's face; Ferro doesn't contradict her, only adds a line to the ledger with a small, satisfied smile before waving you on. Behind you, Senna clutches Corin tighter, whispering thanks that don't quite reach her eyes — the boy's fever-hum hasn't fully stopped, and everyone in the room can still hear the swarm-song threading up faint through the stone, patient as ever, unbothered by anything you took from it tonight.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I don't chase ghosts and silver while people drown, Lieutenant—but the map isn't the only thing burning in these tunnels now, and your jealous second knows it. You want names, you ask the right way, and you better mean it.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts the compel on 'Rumor of Buried Treasure'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: You climb up out of the dark into gray daylight and the familiar clatter of Hollowmoot's market — but the crowd feels wrong today, too many unfamiliar faces lingering near the stalls, watching the crossing points a little too closely. A scarred woman with a Warden's cast-off coat and a coil of rope over her shoulder straightens when she sees Aldous, elbowing the man beside her. Word of silver buried somewhere in the Sallowmere has clearly reached further than any of you intended, and now it's walking around Hollowmoot with knives on its belt, right as you're trying to smuggle a fevered, hive-touched boy through the crowd unnoticed. Senna goes rigid at your side, suddenly torn between two dangers: the quarantine bells, and the strangers asking loud questions about buried treasure and half-burned maps.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Look at me, Senna. I'm getting your son through this safe. The Cartel owes us passage—let me use it.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde immediately steps to Senna's side, reading the room with the sharp precision of someone who's managed crew through dangerous nights—there: the scarred Warden's attention swinging toward Aldous; there: the treasure hunters' hands always close to knife hilts; there: Corin's fever-hum attracting exactly the wrong kind of notice from all around. She catches sight of a familiar Cartel hand emerging from the cellars and meets his eyes with a subtle signal. Then she guides Senna and Corin toward the quieter edges of Hollowmoot's market with the casual confidence of crew doing ordinary work, using her established trust with the Blackwater Cartel to clear a path and move them past the watching eyes.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Stand down, soldier. That boy is marked but not claimed, and he's going north under my watch. You don't want to test what happens if you push this.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps directly into the scarred Warden woman's path with absolute certainty, his weathered frame becoming an immovable barrier between her and Senna. He reads her like he reads omens in floodwater—knows her measure, her intent, the exact pressure point where she'll choose to back down. His voice comes quiet but carries the weight of someone who served under Verrick and understands the Wardens' drill signals in his bones. His hand settles where a weapon might be. He doesn't shout. He never does.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Keep your focus on my voice, Corin, not on the humming—your own breath is stronger than the water's song.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen moves close to the fevered boy immediately, one hand settling on his shoulder as she bends near. Her voice shifts into low, precise syllables—not the elaborate rites from the cellar, but something quieter and more grounding, meant to call his attention back into his own body rather than into the water's song. Her free hand traces a small disrupting pattern above his chest, breaking the rhythm of his humming, pulling his awareness into his own breath, his own heartbeat, his own name. She's read enough hive-touched victims to know exactly how to anchor one who's still half-calling to the deep.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Scarred woman's Warden-marked. We go east through the stalls. Keep Corin between us and keep moving.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire reads the market crowd with the trained precision of checkpoint work, tracking the scarred woman and the fortune hunters circling like birds over the stalls. She signals her companions with the hand signals learned young in the orphanage watch drills, plotting a route through the merchant press that keeps Corin screened between their bodies. Fast, diagonal, no hesitation—just forward momentum through the hunters' attention.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The market swallows you whole and spits you out the other side clean. Ysolde catches the Cartel hand's eye and threads Senna and Corin through a gap in the stalls that looks like nothing more than ordinary crew business — nobody blinks twice. Aldous plants himself in the scarred Warden's path and doesn't say much of anything that isn't already written in the drill-signal set between his shoulders and hers; she reads the warning, reads the certainty behind it, and finds somewhere else to be. Morwen's fingers on Corin's chest break the swarm-song's rhythm clean through — his humming stutters, stumbles, and for the first time since the cellar he's breathing on his own count instead of the water's (**Corin's Song Stilled**). And Mire, reading the crowd like a checkpoint she's already cleared in her head, threads the whole party through a seam in the market's attention that the treasure-hungry strangers never even notice open and close (**A Route Through Unnoticed**). By the time the bells start up somewhere behind you — late, and aimed at nothing — Corin is fevered but himself, Senna has her boy and her route north, and Hollowmoot's watching eyes are all looking the wrong way.

ambiguities.section: §5 (Anatomy of a BEAT card / Procedure step 3)
ambiguities.issue: PLEA FOR HELP has open blanks WHO and WHERE. T-03 (THREAT, table-type HOW) correctly falls back to 'first open blank still empty' = WHO. But F-01 (FACTION, table-type WHO) is drawn second and its matching blank (WHO) is already filled by T-03. §5 step 3 only covers 'matches no open blank' -> first empty blank; it never says what to do when a card's type DOES match an open blank type but that blank is already filled by an earlier draw. The GM resolved this by placing F-01 in the remaining open blank (WHERE) rather than treating it as a fictional mismatch requiring the §11 'doesn't fit' ruling.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table ruling used: when a card's type-matching blank is already filled, treat it the same as a full type mismatch and drop it into the next open blank still empty, in filling order.

ambiguities.section: §7 (Writing triggers / scene loop cleanup step 5) and Backup modules (§7 prep item 3)
ambiguities.issue: Module trigger 'M-2' with condition recorded as 'scene_start:3' fired during scene 2's cleanup step, but its literal condition (scene 3 starting) is an event that had not yet occurred in the play log at time of check (scene 2 had not even formally ended: event 52 trigger precedes event 53 'Scene 2 end'). §7 requires triggers to be checkable from the play log ('an observer could confirm from the play log') at the time they fire, and only defines trigger-checking during the CURRENT scene's cleanup, not for conditions belonging to the next scene. No card reveal, rail addition, or content is logged for whatever M-2 'deployed,' so it's unclear what game effect actually occurred.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table ruling used: treat 'scene_start:N' as shorthand meaning 'about to start scene N,' allowing it to be evaluated one cleanup early with no observable deployment logged since the module's content had not yet been chosen/placed.

ambiguities.issue: The rule says a Story Pile draw triggered by 'a player accepts a compel that did not come from a deck draw' must have its complication 'involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread.' The spec doesn't state whether the pile is drawn before the compel is narrated (so its content can shape the complication) or after (as a consequence). In this log the compel (event 64) was fully narrated and accepted before PS-16 was drawn (events 66-67), so the card could not have informed the complication.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the draw as happening immediately after acceptance, purely to award the GM a free invoke and seed the card for later scenes (it may explain the subsequent Corin/enormous-presence material added to the GM pile at events 87-88), rather than requiring the drawn card's tags to appear in the compel text itself.

ambiguities.issue: The −1 Tension rule explicitly names resolving 'a THREAT or FACTION' or 'filling a player's goal.' The card opposed in this scene's rolls (H-03) is a HAZARD, a type not mentioned in that row. The GM applied −1 at event 84 with note 'resolved,' but the rules don't say overcoming a HAZARD's opposition counts.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated finding Corin (the scene's stated goal) as 'filled a player's goal,' independent of H-03's type, to justify the −1.

The spec says a card 'would exceed the limit' triggers an immediate removal but doesn't specify how many other events may intervene before the discard is logged.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the limit as enforced at the next convenient checkpoint rather than instantaneously on add, with the rail conceptually over-limit in the interim.

ambiguities.issue: The scene-end tension adjustment (event 97) is logged as 'resolved -1' (i.e., 'The party resolved a THREAT or filled a player's goal'), but no event in the scene 4 log shows a roll, a THREAT/FACTION resolution, or any explicit mechanical marker of a goal being filled — the scene consists only of framing and four roleplay/declare rows with no dice, no opposition, and no result. The spec does not define what counts as 'filled a player's goal' in the absence of a roll or clock event.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Treated the GM's narrative judgment (that the party's negotiation resolved the Cartel-promise question posed in the frame) as sufficient grounds for the -1 adjustment, since §6's table does not require a roll specifically, only that a THREAT/FACTION be resolved or a goal be filled.

ambiguities.issue: Two story cards (SN-04 'The Rival Lieutenant', SN-05 'Corin's Fever-Hum Hasn't Stopped') are added directly to a pile via a 'Story card added' event with no preceding draw or Fate-event trigger shown, and no note on which pile (player vs GM) each went to. §6A says new NPCs/threads go to a player's pile 'if it ties to one character, otherwise to the GM Story Pile,' but the log doesn't record that routing decision or its basis.

It does not say whether the full §4 'Resolving a drawn player card' pipeline (offer compel on the weakness tag, surface the card face-up, grant 1 free invoke) also applies to a card drawn this way, since §4's own trigger list for that pipeline names 'the scene test calls for an interrupt' (the Interrupt result) but not the Altered result.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated the Altered-scene draw as also triggering the full §4 player-card resolution: it offered Aldous a compel on PX-21's weakness tag (event 104), then surfaced the card to the rail with 1 free invoke (events 105-106), in addition to using it to color the scene.

In standard Fate, a Create Advantage roll with style does not grant a boost at all -- it grants 2 free invokes on the new aspect instead. The spec does not clarify whether the peek option is available on Create Advantage rolls (where there is no boost to substitute for) or only on roll types (Overcome/Attack) that would normally yield a boost.

Altered-scene narration (market/Warden-woman description) drawn from PX-21 did not reference any of PX-21's power tags or its weakness tag ('whispers of hidden silver', 'draws greedy strangers', 'a half-burned map', 'Treasure Hunters Turn Violent'). Already caught by engine refusal (§6, 'altered scene did not use a tag of the drawn card').
Compel on the surfaced player card correctly used its weakness tag 'Treasure Hunters Turn Violent' per §4 default compel rule.

friction.text: All three Story Pile draws this scene (PS-16, PS-06, PS-05) were logged with the compel's complication text written before the card reveal, inverting §6A's mandated 'reveal then apply' order and making it impossible to confirm the complications actually used the drawn cards' tags.

Aldous's weakness tag 'Panics near deep water' was compelled twice in the same scene (events 11 and 25), concentrating both spotlight and fate-point gain on one player while Mire and Ysolde received none — legal under the rules as written but a notable pacing/spotlight imbalance.

The engine had to refuse a GM attempt to both set difficulty with and invoke L-03's 'Warden watchtower' tag on the same roll (event 32), suggesting the GM-side logic for combining active NPC opposition with face-up GM tags is error-prone at the table.

Beat Frame blank-assignment collision (two GM card types competing for one already-filled blank) is not covered by §5, forcing an unwritten interim ruling that could easily be applied inconsistently across tables.

Story Pile draw (PS-12) triggered correctly on the fiction-only compel, but the log never demonstrates the required tag-usage in the ensuing complication, undermining the 100%-tag-usage metric target from §12.

Cross-scene module trigger timing (M-2 firing on a 'scene_start:3' condition during scene 2's own cleanup, with no visible deployed content) is unaddressed by §7's trigger-writing rules, which only contemplate log-confirmable events that have already happened.

The Story Pile draw for the free-form compel (PS-16) arrived after the complication was already narrated and accepted, so the card had no chance to shape the fiction it's supposed to be tied to — the trigger's timing relative to compel narration needs to be pinned down.

Rail-limit discards lag several events behind the card add that caused the overflow (F-04 added at event 56, T-03 discarded at event 65), leaving the rail silently over its 5-card cap through an entire compel-and-roleplay sequence.

Tension was dropped for 'resolving' a HAZARD card's opposition, but the Tension table's −1 condition only lists THREAT/FACTION, leaving GMs to guess whether HAZARD outcomes and general goal progress qualify.

Tension was decremented at scene end with no roll or clock event in the scene log to visibly ground the '-1: resolved a THREAT / filled a goal' condition, making the ruling hard to audit from the log alone.

The engine refused a Beat Frame/module trigger phrased around 'the party leaves the road or causeway' as not properly evidenced in the play log (§7 trigger-writing rule), indicating prep triggers are still being written too loosely for the 'observer could confirm from the play log' standard.
Story card additions (SN-04, SN-05) don't record which pile (player vs. GM Story Pile) they were filed into, leaving pile bookkeeping implicit rather than logged.

The GM's Altered-scene narration for PX-21 did not actually incorporate any of the card's tags, undercutting the system's core promise that deck draws (not GM improvisation) supply scene specifics; the engine had to flag this twice (§6, §3) before the compel step correctly used the weakness tag.

Overlap between §6's Altered-scene draw and §4's full player-card resolution pipeline (compel + surface + free invoke) is not spelled out, forcing an on-the-spot ruling that a single draw does triple duty (scene color, compel, and surfacing/invoke) -- a structural gap likely to recur every time Tension sits at or near 1.

Two Create Advantage rolls with style (Morwen, Mire) received both the standard 2 free invokes and the Session Deck peek/reorder option, an apparent double-reward stemming from the §3 table's 'instead of a boost' wording not accounting for action types that don't produce a boost in the first place.
